faq.heading: Things tutors have asked
faq.a1_part1: Yes. Data is stored on Supabase infrastructure and payments go through Stripe, so Crestio never sees your card details. Every organisation's data is isolated — no tutor can see another practice's students. Full details in the
faq.q2: What does the AI actually do, and does it train on my data?
faq.a2: The AI polishes your rough session notes into something parents can read clearly. It only sees what you send it in that specific request, doesn't store anything between sessions, and doesn't train on your data. You always keep your original notes — AI polish is optional per session. The provider is certified to SOC 2 Type II.
faq.q3: What happens after the free trial?
faq.a3: Your card gets charged for the plan you chose. Cancel before the trial ends and nothing happens. Cancel after billing starts and you keep access until the end of the period you paid for, then it stops.
faq.a4: Only what you share. Session notes split into internal (yours) and parent-facing (shared). Parents only see sessions you've released to them, and only for their own child.
faq.q5: Is this for tutoring companies or individual tutors?
faq.a5: Both. Solo is for independent tutors. Team fits small tutoring practices up to 5 tutors. Growth supports up to 15. If you're running a larger operation, email support@crestio.ai and we'll point you in the right direction.
faq.a6: The Crestio team is one person — Lenin, founder and HSC English tutor in Sydney. Questions or feedback? Email lenin@crestio.ai and you'll get a reply directly from him, usually within 24 hours.

ai.q: How is the AI different from ChatGPT?
ai.a: Crestio's polish is calibrated to your tutor voice over time and never copies session-to-session — every polish is a fresh request. The model only sees what's needed to write that one update. ChatGPT is a general assistant; this is a specialised tool for tutoring notes.

wrong_polish.q: What if my AI polish sounds wrong?
wrong_polish.a: You review every send. Edit it inline before it goes, or discard the polish entirely and write the parent update yourself. Polish learns from your edits — by the third week, it sounds like you.

pay_optional.a: Yes. You can keep using bank transfer or any other method. Crestio just makes Stripe parent payments easy if you want them — it's not required.

fees.q: What's the Stripe fee on top of Crestio?
fees.a: On parent payments: 2.9% + 30c (Stripe) + 1% (Crestio). Charged to you, not the parent. So on a $100 invoice you keep about $96. No fees on bank-transfer invoices.

export.a: Yes. CSV export of students, sessions, invoices, and messages from Settings → Data. Anytime. No lock-in.

parent_account.a: No. Parents get a private link by email and pay with their card. They can optionally claim an account if they want a history view, but it's never required.

shutdown.a: We commit to 12 months notice and a final export window. Your data stays exportable as CSV the entire time. If we ever do shut down, you'll have plenty of room to migrate.

data.a: Supabase, hosted in Australia for AU customers (or auto-detected closest region for others). Encrypted at rest and in transit. Each organisation's data is isolated — no cross-tenant access at the database level.

about.meta_description: Crestio is built solo, in Sydney, by a working HSC English tutor — for tutors who value their time.
about.heading: Built by a tutor for tutors who give a damn.
about.founder_p1: I started tutoring HSC English in 2021. Within six months I had eight students, a Google Calendar that didn't sync to anything important, an inbox of unread parent texts, and a Sunday-night spreadsheet that took four hours to maintain.
about.founder_p2: I tried every tutoring app I could find. They were either built for tuition centres with 200 students and 30 staff, or they were a calendar app pretending to be tutoring software. None of them were built for the actual hard part: the 9pm parent text, the rough notes that need to become a polite paragraph, the invoice that won't write itself.
about.founder_p3: So I built the thing I needed. Crestio is opinionated about what matters: log a session in 8 seconds, polish your notes the way a parent will read them, get paid by card without learning what Stripe is. Nothing else. No bloat. No upsells. No surprise fees on the parent.
about.founder_p4: If you tutor and you've ever spent a Sunday wishing the admin would do itself — this is for you. Email me directly: lenin@crestio.ai. I read every message.
about.values_calm_body: No streaks, no badges, no notification bombs. The app is quiet so you can hear yourself think.
about.values_tutor_body: We don't sell to schools or chains. Every product decision asks: would a working tutor with eight students actually use this — or is it just busywork dressed up as a feature?
about.values_privacy_body: Parents see what you share, nothing more. AI never trains on your data. Tutors in a team can't see each other's rates.
about.values_built_body: We ship the changelog. We email customers when something changes. We tell you what's broken before you find it.
about.why_p1: Tutoring software is a graveyard of products built by people who never tutored. The tools that exist optimise for the tuition-centre owner with 50 staff, not the working tutor with eight students and a Sunday admin block.
about.why_p2: We built Crestio because tutors deserve the same software craft that designers, developers, and writers get. Calm tools, sharp typography, fast keyboard shortcuts, real product care.
about.why_p3: And because the work tutors do — paying attention to one kid, planning the next session, writing notes a parent will actually read — is worth doing well. The admin around it should never be the hard part.
about.roadmap_body: We ship every week or two. The public changelog is the source of truth.
about.hiring_heading: We don't have open roles right now.
about.hiring_body: We will. When we do, they'll be listed here. No surprise listings, no "send your CV anyway" inbox.
about.contact_intro: Questions, feedback, ideas? We read every message.
about.body_1: Crestio is built solo, in Sydney, by a working HSC English tutor.
about.body_2: We think the work tutors do is the part that should get your time.
about.body_3: So Crestio is opinionated. It does the boring parts well, gets out of the way for the rest, and gives you something quiet and well-made to use every day.

music_teachers.heading: Light, honest software for music teachers.
music_teachers.sub: Crestio supports music teachers via free-text subjects and session notes. Log what was covered, polish it for the parent, invoice at the end of the week. The instrument-specific stuff — recital scheduling, repertoire databases, exam grade progressions — Crestio doesn't have yet.
music_teachers.micro: Free-text session notes · AI polish · card payments
music_teachers.pain_heading: Music teaching has its own admin.
music_teachers.pain_1: You finish a piano lesson and need to write the parent in two minutes — but you taught five kids today and they're blurring together.
music_teachers.pain_2: Parents want to know what piece their child is on — you tell them, then forget you told them, then tell them again.
music_teachers.pain_3: Invoices for the term lag behind because you're focused on next week's lesson, not last week's billing.
music_teachers.pain_4: Half your students are mid-grade and half are beginner — your notes mix together.
music_teachers.resolution: Crestio's per-student session notes and AI-polished parent updates handle the part that's the same for every tutor.
music_teachers.limitations_heading: What Crestio doesn't do for music teachers.
music_teachers.limitations_intro: Honest list of things music teachers sometimes need that Crestio does not handle today:
music_teachers.limitations_b1: No instrument library or repertoire database.
music_teachers.limitations_b2: No recital scheduler or ticket sales.
music_teachers.limitations_b3: No exam grade tracker (AMEB, ABRSM, Trinity, RCM, etc.).
music_teachers.limitations_b4: No practice-time logging app for students.
music_teachers.limitations_b5: No sheet music storage as a structured library — you can attach PDFs to sessions, but not browse a catalogue.
music_teachers.limitations_closing: If those would change your decision, email lenin@crestio.ai. They're not on the roadmap right now.
music_teachers.faq_1_q: Can I log what was practised in each session?
music_teachers.faq_1_a: Yes. Each session has a free-text notes field — write what you covered, what to practise this week, and what's on for next time. Polish converts that into a parent-friendly update.
music_teachers.faq_2_q: Does Crestio have a recital scheduler or ticket sales?
music_teachers.faq_2_a: No. There's no recital event type and no ticket sales. You can use a session at a custom date as a placeholder, but if you run regular recitals you'll want a separate tool. TutorBird is the closest fit for music-school operations.
music_teachers.faq_3_q: Can I share sheet music PDFs with parents?
music_teachers.faq_3_a: Yes — attach a PDF to a session or a student. Parents view it watermarked through the portal. There's no library view; PDFs live alongside the session or student you attached them to.

exam_prep.heading: Built for exam years.

new_tutors.mistakes_1: Forgetting to send a session summary. Parents stop trusting you within two weeks.
new_tutors.mistakes_2: Letting unpaid invoices pile up. Address them within a week or you'll never get paid.
new_tutors.mistakes_3: Charging less than you should because you feel new. Set a fair rate, raise it once you have 5 students.
new_tutors.mistakes_4: Doing all your notes in one Sunday block. Log as you go. Polish later.
new_tutors.cta_heading: Try the thing tutors with eight students wish they'd had on day one.
